title: Tolosa to San José 1111: the Law Student, the Sash, and the Balcony Under House Arrest
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Tolosa and the Faculty of Law

stops.name: Tolosa, La Plata: the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested; en.wikipedia and es.wikipedia agree on 19 February 1953. One entry in the gathered pool gave 1954 and contradicted its own chronology; 1953 stands. The coordinate is corrected from the supplied La Plata city centre to Tolosa proper, per es.wikipedia 'Tolosa (La Plata)'
stops.campa: In Tolosa, a railway barrio on the northern edge of La Plata, Ofelia Esther Wilhelm bears a daughter and names her Cristina Elisabet. The father, Eduardo Fernández, drives a colectivo. The mother works for the provincial tax office and will rise to general secretary of her union. The city around the cradle is seventy years old, a grid crossed by diagonals, reasoned into existence by men who believed a capital could be designed; Julio Argentino Roca inaugurated it in 1882. No source reachable names the clinic. The daughter born here will hold the presidency twice and be forbidden it for life.
suggested_refs: The barrio of Tolosa, La Plata partido, three kilometres northwest of the Plaza Moreno axis

stops.name: Facultad de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales, La Plata: two law students
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1973; no enrolment month is given in any reachable source, defaulted to January
stops.campa: She enrolls in law at the Universidad Nacional de La Plata in a year when the faculties are less lecture halls than assemblies. Perón is coming back from eighteen years in Madrid, and the Peronist Youth fills the corridors with columns, drums, and mimeographed positions. Among the law students is Néstor Carlos Kirchner, from Río Gallegos at the far end of the country, thin and argumentative and two thousand kilometres from home. They meet here. Neither of them finishes the degree on schedule.
suggested_refs: The Facultad de Ciencias Jurídicas y Sociales of the UNLP, calle 48 between 6 and 7
sources: Argentine press biographies of both Kirchners

stops.name: Puente 12, on the road from Ezeiza: the guns at Perón's return
stops.date_confidence: attested for the event; her own presence is reconstruction [R], asserted by some journalistic retrospectives and uncorroborated by others. Coordinate corrected from Ezeiza airport to the actual shooting site at Puente 12, per en.wikipedia 'Ezeiza massacre'
stops.campa: The crowd walks out the General Ricchieri freeway to meet Perón's plane, and where the road crosses the Camino de Cintura, at the bridge they call Puente 12, the armed right of the movement opens fire on the columns of its left. The dead are counted in the dozens. Some accounts of her youth put the two law students in that crowd; other accounts do not corroborate it. The fracture opened here runs through the movement she will one day preside over. José López Rega, standing behind the old man, is already assembling the Triple A.
suggested_refs: The junction of the Ricchieri freeway and the Camino de Cintura, ten kilometres from the Ezeiza terminal
sources: Disputed journalistic retrospectives on her presence

stops.name: La Plata: the civil marriage
stops.date_confidence: disputed and left standing: es.wikipedia gives Thursday 8 May 1975, and 8 May 1975 was in fact a Thursday; en.wikipedia gives 9 May 1975. The pool's [A] tag overstated it. No reachable source names the registry office, so the pin is the La Plata city coordinate already canonical in the atlas
stops.campa: They marry in a civil ceremony in La Plata, students still, without a named venue in any source anyone can reach. She is twenty-two. He is twenty-five. Argentina is a year from the coup that will take thirty thousand people out of their houses. López Rega's Triple A is already killing the generation the two of them organized with in the faculty corridors, and within a year and a half the couple will be at the other end of the continent, in a windy port town where nobody is looking for them.
suggested_refs: The 1975 civil registry books of the partido de La Plata, venue unidentified in reachable sources

stops.name: La Plata: the title of procuradora
stops.date_confidence: attested, es.wikipedia. Replaces the pool's 1976-07-03, a date appearing in no reachable source, and corrects its framing: the procuradora title precedes the move south rather than following it
stops.campa: Three subjects short of the full degree, she takes the intermediate title of procuradora at the Universidad Nacional de La Plata. Twenty-three days later the junta takes the Casa Rosada. The three missing subjects will sit unwritten for three and a half years while the couple builds a practice at the end of the world, and the last of them, Derecho Internacional Privado, will be sat in October 1979 by a woman who by then has a child, a law firm, and a province she is learning to read.
suggested_refs: The UNLP academic record for the procuradora title, 21 April 1976

stops.name: Río Gallegos: the firm of Kirchner y Kirchner
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1976 in biographical press; the month is not given in reachable sources and is defaulted
stops.campa: The couple moves to Néstor's home town on the estuary of the Gallegos river, seventy-six years after Juan Perón's family came south to the sheep estancias of this same province. They open a joint practice, Kirchner y Kirchner, and work real estate and civil matters through the dictatorship, foreclosures and mortgages in a town of wind and corrugated iron. It is the least conspicuous address in Argentina, and both of the careers that follow are run out of it for more than a decade.
suggested_refs: The offices of Kirchner y Kirchner, Río Gallegos, active through the years of the junta
sources: Biographical press coverage of both Kirchners
juan_peron.journey.json (Río Gallegos, the estancias of the far south, 1900)

stops.name: La Plata: the birth of Máximo
stops.date_confidence: contradiction flagged, not resolved: es.wikipedia 'Máximo Kirchner' gives 16 February 1977 at La Plata, Buenos Aires Province; the gathered pool gave 23 February 1977 at Río Gallegos. The es.wikipedia CFK article says only 'nacido en febrero de 1977'. The La Plata birthplace also undercuts the claim that the couple had already settled south
stops.campa: Her first child is born, and named Máximo. The Spanish record puts the birth in La Plata, the city she came from; other accounts put it in Río Gallegos, the city she went to. Both cannot stand, and neither is set aside here. The child will grow into a national deputy and the head of La Cámpora, the organization that carries her name into a generation born after the sash. In February 1977 he is a week old and the country is disappearing people at a rate no one is yet permitted to count.
suggested_refs: The Argentine civil registry entry for Máximo Carlos Kirchner, February 1977

stops.name: Río Gallegos: admitted to the bar of Santa Cruz
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1980 for the Santa Cruz registration; the completion of the abogacía on 1 October 1979 is attested by es.wikipedia. Neither has a reachable day for the registration, defaulted
stops.campa: On the first of October 1979 she sits Derecho Internacional Privado at La Plata and the degree is finished, four years late and entirely on her own terms. The following year she registers as a practicing attorney in Santa Cruz, the smallest bar in the country by number and the largest by distance. She is not a first lady who read law; she is a lawyer who married one. The trials that come forty years later are argued by a defendant who reads her own file and drafts her own answer to it.
suggested_refs: The roll of the Colegio de Abogados of Santa Cruz, admissions of 1980

stops.name: Legislatura de Santa Cruz, Río Gallegos: the first seat
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1989 in the Argentine electoral and biographical record; no month reachable, defaulted
stops.campa: She is elected provincial deputy for Santa Cruz, and the elected career begins here, in a chamber small enough that every member knows every other member's mortgage. Néstor is mayor of Río Gallegos. The two careers are run out of one house and one province. Buenos Aires does not notice. Buenos Aires has hyperinflation, supermarket lootings, and a president handing over five months early, and the far south is a rounding error in the national accounts.
suggested_refs: The Cámara de Diputados of Santa Cruz Province, sessions of 1989

stops.name: Casa de Gobierno de Santa Cruz, Río Gallegos: the interim governorship
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1990 for the interim governorship following the impeachment of Ricardo del Val; no month reachable, defaulted. The 1991 campaign described in the campa is attested to that year
stops.campa: Governor Ricardo del Val is impeached and she holds the governorship briefly, in the interim, the first executive office of her life and one nobody elected her to. The following year she runs Néstor's campaign for the same building and wins it for him. He will hold it three terms. She will spend those twelve years in provincial and then national legislative seats tied to Santa Cruz. One Kirchner sits in an executive and one sits in a chamber, and the pair hold to that arrangement until 2007.
suggested_refs: The Casa de Gobierno of Santa Cruz Province, Río Gallegos
sources: Standard political biography of the Kirchner governorship period

stops.name: Río Gallegos: the birth of Florencia
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction [R]: standard biographical record, not independently confirmed against a registry entry in any reachable source
stops.campa: Her second child is born and named Florencia. The father is governor-elect of nothing yet; the mother has just handed back an interim governorship she held by accident of impeachment. The daughter will grow up inside the Casa Rosada years, will be photographed as an adolescent at state funerals, and will spend a stretch of her adulthood in Havana under medical treatment while her mother is prosecuted at home. In September 1990 she is a birth certificate in a town of thirty thousand.
suggested_refs: The civil registry of Río Gallegos, September 1990
sources: Standard biographical record, tagged [R] in the verified pool

stops.name: Santa Fe: the constitutional convention
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1994; the convention sat at Santa Fe and Paraná between May and August, and no precise session date for her is in the reachable pool
stops.campa: She is elected a delegate to the assembly that rewrites the Argentine Constitution, and sits in Santa Fe among the men negotiating Menem's re-election into the text of the country. The convention shortens the presidential term, permits one consecutive re-election, and creates the office of Chief of Cabinet. Thirteen years later she will be sworn in under this constitution, and seventeen years after that a court will invoke the office it created to disqualify her from ever holding office again.
suggested_refs: The 1994 Constituent Convention, sitting at Santa Fe and Paraná

stops.name: Congreso Nacional, Buenos Aires: senator for Santa Cruz
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1995; the 10 December seating date is the standard Argentine legislative calendar rather than a separately sourced fact
stops.campa: She takes a seat in the Senate of the Nation for Santa Cruz, and the far south sends its lawyer to the capital. In the chamber she becomes what the province never had room for: an orator, in a body that mostly negotiates in corridors. Domingo Faustino Sarmiento swore the presidential oath in this city in October 1868, in a Congress that had not yet built this palace; Juan Perón swore his here in June 1946. She is forty-two and nobody yet writes her name without her husband's beside it.
suggested_refs: The Palacio del Congreso de la Nación Argentina, Senate chamber
sources: sarmiento.journey.json (Buenos Aires, the oath of office, 1868-10-12)

stops.name: Congreso Nacional, Buenos Aires: out of the bloc, and back
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1997 for the removal from the bloc, the resignation, and the run for deputy; no month reachable, defaulted. The 2001 Senate victory described in the campa is attested to that year
stops.campa: The Justicialist bloc removes her over an internal misconduct dispute; she resigns the seat and runs instead for national deputy in the midterms. Peronism does this to its own and then takes them back. In 2001, the year the country burns through five presidents in a fortnight and the banks close on everyone's savings, Santa Cruz elects her senator again. She is expelled and returned inside four years, and for the next quarter century she argues that the institutions expelling her are the ones acting outside the rules.
suggested_refs: The Justicialist Senate bloc proceedings of 1997; the Santa Cruz senatorial result of 2001

stops.name: Congreso Nacional, Buenos Aires: Néstor takes the oath
stops.date_confidence: attested. Venue corrected: the pool placed the swearing-in at the Casa Rosada, but per en.wikipedia 'Néstor Kirchner' the oath is taken before the Legislative Assembly at the Palace of the Argentine National Congress, with the sash and staff handed over afterwards at the Casa Rosada
stops.campa: Néstor Kirchner takes the presidential oath before the Legislative Assembly with twenty-two percent of the first round behind him and no second round, because Menem withdrew rather than lose one. She stands beside him and becomes First Lady of a country that has just defaulted on ninety-three billion dollars. They walk afterwards to the Casa Rosada for the sash and the staff, into the building where Perón was sworn in in 1946, where Isabel Perón took the vice presidency in 1973, and where Licio Gelli was decorated the same year.
suggested_refs: The Legislative Assembly session of 25 May 2003 and the transfer of the attributes at Balcarce 50

stops.name: La Plata: against Chiche Duhalde
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 2005; the legislative election was held on 23 October 2005, a date from the standard electoral calendar rather than separately sourced in the pool
stops.campa: She leaves Santa Cruz behind and runs for the Senate in Buenos Aires Province, the biggest electorate in the country, against Hilda González de Duhalde, wife of the president who handed power to her husband. She wins. Kirchnerism stops being a Patagonian franchise and takes the conurbano, and her own name stands at the head of a ballot for the first time. The province she now represents contains the barrio she was born in, and the university where two law students met over a mimeograph in 1973.
suggested_refs: The Buenos Aires Province senatorial result of October 2005

stops.name: Buenos Aires: forty-five percent
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: She wins the presidency outright in the first round with about forty-five percent, more than twenty points clear of the second place. Her husband, the sitting president, does not run. Nothing in Argentine constitutional practice forbids the arrangement and nothing in Argentine political memory has seen it: a president handing the office to his wife by election rather than by death, as Perón's was handed to Isabel in 1974 by a heart stopping in the Quinta de Olivos. The country calls the arrangement a relay and votes for it anyway.
suggested_refs: The Argentine general election of 28 October 2007

stops.name: Congreso Nacional, Buenos Aires: the oath of the tenth of December
stops.date_confidence: attested. Venue corrected as at her husband's inauguration: the oath is taken before the Legislative Assembly in the Congress building, not at the Casa Rosada, though the pool placed it there
stops.campa: She is sworn in as the fifty-fifth President of Argentina, the first woman elected to the office rather than inheriting it from a husband's corpse. Isabel Perón, sworn in as vice president at the Casa Rosada in October 1973, was the first woman to hold executive power here and did not stand for it. This is the second, and this one was voted. The sash passes from the outgoing president to the incoming one, and for the only time in the country's history the two of them go home to the same house.
suggested_refs: The presidential inauguration of 10 December 2007 before the Legislative Assembly
sources: isabel_peron.journey.json (Casa Rosada, sworn in as vice president, 1973-10-12)

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Buenos Aires: Resolution 125
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 2008 for the resolution; the 11 March date is the commonly reported issue date and is not separately confirmed in the reachable pool
stops.campa: Her government issues a sliding-scale export tax on grain and oilseed, indexed so that the state takes more as the price rises. The countryside stops the country. Roadblocks close the routes for a hundred days, the cities empty of beef, and the confrontation between the pampa and the Casa Rosada becomes the defining quarrel of her first term. In April the economy minister, Martín Lousteau, resigns in the middle of it. In July the Senate splits and her own vice president votes the resolution down.
suggested_refs: Resolution 125/2008 of the Ministry of Economy and the hundred-day farm conflict

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the Universal Child Allowance
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 2009 only; the specific decree date is not in the verified pool and is not asserted here. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Her government creates the Asignación Universal por Hijo, a monthly payment to the children of the unemployed and the informally employed, conditional on school attendance and vaccination. It reaches millions of children within a year. No reachable source gives the date of the decree, only the year. Governments that dismantle the rest of her programme leave this line of the ledger standing, and her own later letters return to it as the evidence that what is being prosecuted is a project and not a person.
suggested_refs: The Asignación Universal por Hijo, created 2009

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Buenos Aires: the bicentennial fund and the Central Bank
stops.date_confidence: attested for DNU 18/2010 of 7 January 2010. The pool conflated two events into January 2010: the Fondo del Bicentenario was created by DNU in December 2009 (DNU 2010/09), and Redrado then resigned on 29 January 2010, his removal confirmed by a bicameral commission on 3 February 2010 per es.wikipedia 'Martín Redrado'
stops.campa: In December she creates a bicentennial fund by decree, to pay foreign debt out of Central Bank reserves. The bank's president, Martín Redrado, refuses to transfer them. On the seventh of January a second decree removes him; he does not go, the courts intervene, and he resigns at the end of the month while a bicameral commission argues over whether a president may fire a central banker at all. It is the first open constitutional fight of her presidency, and it sets the order of the ones that follow: a decree, a refusal, a court.
suggested_refs: DNU 2010/09 creating the Fondo del Bicentenario and DNU 18/2010 removing Martín Redrado

stops.name: El Calafate: the death of Néstor Kirchner
stops.date_confidence: discrepancy flagged rather than silently resolved: one fetched Wikipedia extraction in the pool listed 23 October 2010; the widely reported death date is 27 October 2010, used here
stops.campa: In their house at El Calafate, under the ice fields, Néstor Kirchner's heart stops. He is sixty and has been out of the presidency for less than three years, president of his party, deputy, and the man everyone assumes will run again in 2011. She is at El Calafate with him, president and widow inside the same hour, and receives the news where there is no one to receive it from. The country hears at mid-morning. She comes north with the body on a national aircraft that afternoon.
suggested_refs: The Kirchner residence at El Calafate, Santa Cruz
sources: Extensive Argentine and international press, October 2010

stops.name: Casa Rosada, Buenos Aires: the body lies in state
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The coffin is set in the Salón de los Patriotas Latinoamericanos and the line to pass it runs out into the Plaza de Mayo and back along the avenues for blocks, in rain, for a day and a night. Perón addressed the descamisados from the balcony above this courtyard on the seventeenth of October 1945; Licio Gelli was decorated inside this building in May 1973. The widow stands beside the coffin and receives the country one person at a time. She will address crowds from that balcony repeatedly for five more years, and the crowd will never again be as large as this queue.
suggested_refs: The lying-in-state at the Casa Rosada, 28 October 2010
sources: juan_peron.journey.json (Plaza de Mayo, the balcony and the descamisados, 1945-10-17)

stops.name: Río Gallegos: the burial and the mausoleum
stops.date_confidence: attested. The apparent contradiction in the pool between a cemetery plot and a family mausoleum resolves as a sequence rather than a conflict: interment in the Río Gallegos municipal cemetery in October 2010, transfer to the purpose-built family mausoleum in 2011
stops.campa: The cortege goes south to Río Gallegos and he is buried in the municipal cemetery of the town where the practice was opened in 1976, a kilometre from the office, in the province Juan Perón's family came to in 1900 for the sheep. The following year the body is moved into a mausoleum built for it, and the accounts that disagree about cemetery or mausoleum are simply reading two different years. She returns north alone to a presidency with fourteen months left in it and no partner in the arrangement that made it.
suggested_refs: The Mausoleum of Néstor Kirchner, Río Gallegos, completed 2011
sources: juan_peron.journey.json (Río Gallegos, the estancias of the far south, 1900-06-01)

stops.name: Congreso Nacional, Buenos Aires: fifty-four percent and the second oath
stops.date_confidence: attested for both the 23 October 2011 election result of 54.11 percent and the 10 December 2011 inauguration
stops.campa: In October she is re-elected with fifty-four point one one percent, the widest margin since the return of democracy, a year and four days after the death that the country widely credits with widening it. On the tenth of December she takes the oath a second time, in black. She governs now without the man who built the arrangement with her, and the second term will be conducted against the currency, the courts, the Church, the press, and eventually the street, all at once and mostly by decree.
suggested_refs: The Argentine general election of 23 October 2011 and the inauguration of 10 December 2011

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the cepo cambiario
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 2012; the controls were tightened progressively across the year and the pool gives no single date, so month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: Her government closes the country's access to foreign currency: authorization required to buy dollars, quantities rationed against declared income, the tax agency standing between a citizen and a hundred-dollar bill. The country names it the cepo, the stocks. A parallel exchange rate opens within weeks and never closes again. For the rest of her term the gap between the official dollar and the blue dollar is the number the country reads first, and her successors campaign on it.
suggested_refs: The foreign exchange restrictions of 2012 and the parallel dollar market

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the eighth of November
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: In September the pots come out against a proposed constitutional amendment that would let her run a third time. On the eighth of November they come out again in a demonstration the press calls 8N, an estimated crowd approaching five hundred thousand in Buenos Aires alone, converging on the obelisk and the Plaza de Mayo. Nothing is broken and nothing is conceded. The amendment does not proceed. The country has discovered that it can assemble half a million people against her without a party, a union, or a leader, and it will do it again in April.
suggested_refs: The 8N cacerolazo of 8 November 2012

stops.name: Caracas: the vigil for Chávez
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the pool placed her in the 8 March funeral procession to the Academia Militar. Per en.wikipedia 'Death and state funeral of Hugo Chávez' she was among the first heads of state to arrive, on 5 March 2013, paid respects at the military hospital chapel, and returned home before the 8 March state funeral. Recorded as a 5 to 7 March visit
stops.campa: Hugo Chávez dies and she is among the first heads of state on the ground in Caracas, arriving the same day. She goes to the chapel at the military hospital where the body lies and stands there with the Venezuelan command. She flies home before the state funeral itself. The bloc she belongs to loses its centre of gravity. The alignment Fidel Castro anchored in Havana, which had refused thirty billion dollars of Argentine reparations in 1959 and been courted by every government since, contracts from this year onward.
suggested_refs: The military hospital chapel, Caracas, March 2013
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Hugo Chávez'
fidel_castro.journey.json (Buenos Aires: thirty billion dollars, refused, 1959-05-01)

stops.name: Vatican, Apostolic Palace: the Argentine pope
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Five days after the conclave she is received by Francis, the first Argentine pope, a man she had spent a decade at odds with when he was Cardinal Bergoglio of Buenos Aires and her government was legalizing same-sex marriage over his objection. She asks him to intervene on the Malvinas. He gives her a kiss on the cheek and the photograph goes around the world. From this audience forward the most powerful Argentine alive is a Jesuit in Rome, and both of them behave as though the quarrel had been someone else's.
suggested_refs: The papal audience of 18 March 2013, days after the election of Francis

stops.name: La Plata: the water
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 2013 for the flooding of Buenos Aires and La Plata; the 2 April date is the commonly reported onset in La Plata and is not separately confirmed in the reachable pool
stops.campa: Four hundred millimetres of rain fall on La Plata in a night and the city she was born in goes under. Dozens drown in basements and on ground floors; the official count is contested for years afterward. In the same weeks her government announces a package of judicial reform, elected magistrates' councils and limits on injunctions against the state, and the country reads the two events together because they arrive together. The reform is struck down in part by the Supreme Court in June.
suggested_refs: The La Plata flood of April 2013 and the judicial reform package of the same weeks

stops.name: Buenos Aires: Nisman
stops.date_confidence: attested for the death on 18 January 2015. The pool folded the 18F silent march into the same entry; that march was weeks later, on 18 February 2015, and is kept distinct here
stops.campa: Alberto Nisman, the federal prosecutor of the AMIA bombing, is found dead in his bathroom in Puerto Madero the night before he is to appear before Congress and accuse her of covering up Iranian responsibility in exchange for trade. A pistol is beside him. Suicide and murder are both argued from the first hour and are still argued. A month later, in silence and in rain, prosecutors lead a march of hundreds of thousands that the country calls 18F. Her last year in office is conducted with a dead accuser in the room.
suggested_refs: The death of prosecutor Alberto Nisman, 18 January 2015, and the 18F silent march of 18 February 2015

stops.name: Great Hall of the People, Beijing: the agreements
stops.date_confidence: year corrected: the pool dated this February 2014, but per en.wikipedia 'Argentina-China relations' the state visit and the accompanying trade, infrastructure and defence agreements are February 2015. Xi's own visit to Argentina was July 2014. The precise day within February is not in the reachable pool and is approximate
stops.campa: Shut out of international credit markets by the New York courts and the holdout creditors her government refuses to pay, she goes to Beijing and signs a package of trade, infrastructure and defence agreements in the Great Hall of the People: dams in Santa Cruz, railway stock, a currency swap, a deep space station in Neuquén operated by the Chinese army. The financing Washington will not extend, Beijing will. The strategy of the last term is to owe the debt to somebody else.
suggested_refs: The February 2015 Argentina-China state visit agreements signed at the Great Hall of the People

stops.name: Plaza de Mayo, Buenos Aires: the last balcony
stops.date_confidence: attested to 9 and 10 December 2015; she declined the formal handover on the tenth, and the balcony address to supporters is dated to the eve of the transfer in the reported record
stops.campa: She will not hand the sash to Mauricio Macri in person. The two sides litigate the protocol of the transfer in court, which has never happened here before, and she goes instead to the balcony over the Plaza de Mayo, the balcony Perón used in October 1945, and speaks to the crowd below as a private citizen from tomorrow. Then she leaves the building for the last time as its president. Twelve years of Kirchner governments end, and no photograph exists of the sash changing hands.
stops.quote: No bajen los brazos. No permitan que les roben la esperanza.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Carta abierta: El costo democrático de la politización de la justicia', cfkargentina.com, 29 July 2026 (written eleven years later; placed here for what it addresses)
suggested_refs: The balcony address of 9 December 2015 and the litigated protocol of the transfer
sources: juan_peron.journey.json (Plaza de Mayo, the balcony and the descamisados)

stops.name: Instituto Patria, Buenos Aires: the base out of office
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2016 onward; no founding day is given in the reachable pool and the date is defaulted
stops.campa: Out of power for the first time in twelve years, she establishes herself in a building on the avenue Rivadavia and calls it the Instituto Patria. Deputies, ministers without ministries, young organizers, and lawyers pass through it. For the years of the Macri government it is the operational centre of Kirchnerism, a shadow cabinet that meets in a foundation because parties are not where the movement lives. From here she runs the argument she will make for the next decade: that the prosecutions now arriving are an election continued by other means.
stops.quote: impedir que los pueblos gobiernen su propio destino
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Mensaje en las Jornadas internacionales Lawfare, la estrategia regional del nuevo golpe de Estado', cfkargentina.com, 13 November 2025
suggested_refs: The Instituto Patria, Buenos Aires, operational centre of Kirchnerism from 2016

stops.name: Senado de la Nación, Buenos Aires: the seat and the warrant
stops.date_confidence: attested for the seating on 10 December 2017 and for the 2017 arrest warrant on the treason charge in the Iran memorandum case. The quoted audio is dated 12 March 2017, corrected from the pool's erroneous 'Perfil and El Liberal, January 2017' after a first-generation Ambito account was fetched directly
stops.campa: A judge issues an arrest warrant against her on a charge of treason, for the memorandum of understanding signed with Iran over the AMIA bombing. She is senator-elect for Buenos Aires Province. Parliamentary immunity attaches on the tenth of December and the warrant cannot be executed, and the Senate declines to strip it. From this year the two calendars run in parallel and never separate again: the electoral one, which keeps returning her to office, and the judicial one, which keeps preparing to remove her from it.
stops.quote: Hay que salir a apretar a los jueces
stops.quote_source: Leaked audio of Cristina Fernández de Kirchner to Oscar Parrilli, broadcast on La Cornisa and reported by Ámbito, La Nación and Télam, 12 March 2017; press reporting of a recording she has not acknowledged as a transcript
suggested_refs: The 2017 treason indictment in the Iran memorandum case and the Senate immunity vote

stops.name: La Rural, Buenos Aires: Sinceramente at the Book Fair
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate corrected: the pool gave a point in Nuñez-Saavedra about 4.5 km from the venue; the fair is held at La Rural, Predio Ferial de Buenos Aires, at 34 degrees 34 minutes 43 seconds south, 58 degrees 25 minutes 15 seconds west
stops.campa: She announces the book on Twitter on the twenty-third of April and it is in shops on the twenty-fifth: five hundred and ninety-four pages, ten chapters and an epilogue, written over a year with the drafts carried between people on USB sticks rather than sent by email, because she assumes the email is read. Sixty thousand copies go in a week and a third printing passes two hundred and ten thousand by the first of May. At the Book Fair the hall will not hold the crowd and the organizers rig screens outside. The book tour is the campaign.
suggested_refs: Sinceramente, Editorial Sudamericana, 2019; the Feria del Libro presentation of 9 May 2019 at La Rural

stops.name: Congreso Nacional, Buenos Aires: sworn as vice president
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: She puts her own former chief of cabinet at the head of the ticket and takes the second place herself. Alberto Fernández is elected and she is sworn in as the thirty-seventh Vice President of Argentina, which makes her the second woman in that office after Isabel Perón took it in October 1973. The immunity of the Senate presidency comes with it. A former president returns to the building she was twice inaugurated in, one chair to the left of where she sat before.
suggested_refs: The vice presidential inauguration of 10 December 2019
sources: isabel_peron.journey.json (Casa Rosada, sworn in as vice president, 1973-10-12)

stops.name: Havana: the book abroad
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 2020 for the Havana International Book Fair presentation; no day is given in the reachable pool and is defaulted
stops.campa: Sinceramente is presented outside Argentina for the first time at the Havana International Book Fair, six weeks into her vice presidency, in a city she has come to repeatedly and where her daughter has been treated. Fidel Castro has been three years in the ground at Santa Ifigenia. The pink tide that carried her governments is down to a handful of capitals. She presents a memoir about being prosecuted, and in this city the argument needs no translation.
suggested_refs: The Feria Internacional del Libro de La Habana, February 2020
sources: fidel_castro.journey.json (Santa Ifigenia Cemetery, Santiago de Cuba: one word, 2016-12-04)

stops.name: Recoleta, Buenos Aires: the gun that does not fire
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate corrected to the point given by en.wikipedia's article on the attempt, 34 degrees 35 minutes 34 seconds south, 58 degrees 23 minutes 15 seconds west; the pool's geography entry was about 570 m off and inconsistent with its own afterlife entry
stops.campa: She is signing books for the crowd outside her building when Fernando André Sabag Montiel reaches over the heads with a Bersa Lusber 84, puts the muzzle inches from her face, and pulls the trigger twice. The magazine holds five cartridges. The chamber is empty. She does not hear it and does not flinch, and the crowd takes him down. He carries Nazi tattoos and prior arrests for carrying a knife. Plaza de Mayo fills the next day, declared a national holiday in repudiation, and a court will give him ten years in October 2025.
suggested_refs: The Bersa Lusber 84 recovered at Juncal and Uruguay, loaded with five cartridges and no round chambered
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Attempted assassination of Cristina Fernández de Kirchner'

stops.name: Comodoro Py, Buenos Aires: the Vialidad sentence
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The judges of the Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal N.2 read the verdict in the road-works case: guilty of fraudulent administration, six years in prison, and disqualification from public office for life. She is vice president of the republic while it is read, and immune from the prison for as long as she holds an office the sentence forbids her to hold. She answers the same afternoon that she will not be a candidate for any office at the next election.
stops.quote: transformaron la justicia y el poder judicial en un verdadero instrumento de disciplinamiento político
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Mensaje en las Jornadas internacionales Lawfare, la estrategia regional del nuevo golpe de Estado', cfkargentina.com, 13 November 2025
suggested_refs: The Vialidad verdict of the Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal Federal N.2, 6 December 2022

stops.name: Buenos Aires: out of office, head of the party
stops.date_confidence: attested for the assumption of the Justicialist Party presidency on 17 November 2024 and for the end of the vice presidency on 10 December 2023
stops.campa: She leaves the vice presidency in December 2023, in the week Javier Milei takes the Casa Rosada with a chainsaw for a campaign emblem, out of every office for the first time since 1989. Eleven months later the Justicialist Party elects her its president, with José Mayans as vice, and the appellate court has by then upheld her conviction. She takes command of Peronism at the moment the sentence forbids her from ever standing for anything again, which is the arrangement she spends the following two years describing as the point of the sentence.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Mensaje a mis compañeros y compañeras en el Día de la Lealtad Peronista', cfkargentina.com, 17 October 2025
suggested_refs: The Partido Justicialista leadership election of 17 November 2024

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the Supreme Court confirms
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 2025 for the Corte Suprema ruling upholding the Vialidad conviction and the lifetime ban; the pool gives the month only and the day here is approximate
stops.campa: The Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación declines the appeal and the Vialidad conviction becomes final: six years, and disqualification from public office for the rest of her life. Twelve years earlier her government had proposed electing the magistrates' council by popular vote and this court had struck the reform down. She had helped write the constitution these judges apply, at Santa Fe in 1994. The sentence is now enforceable and there is no office left standing between her and it.
stops.quote: convertir al Derecho y al Sistema de Justicia en un arma política para eliminar adversarios que no pudieron ser derrotados por el voto
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Carta abierta: El costo democrático de la politización de la justicia', cfkargentina.com, 29 July 2026
suggested_refs: The Corte Suprema ruling of June 2025 confirming the Vialidad conviction

stops.name: San José 1111, Buenos Aires: house arrest
stops.date_confidence: attested for the house arrest beginning 17 June 2025; the street address is [R], commonly reported in the Argentine press but not confirmed here, since the Infobae article on the apartment returned HTTP 404 on fetch
stops.campa: She begins her sentence at home, in an apartment in Constitución, with an electronic monitor on her ankle and a court-set list of who may come up the stairs. The street below fills, and keeps filling, on the days the calendar gives it a reason. She comes out onto the balcony and speaks down into it. Perón used a balcony over the Plaza de Mayo in October 1945 and she used the same one until December 2015; this one is four floors up over a narrow street in a neighbourhood of pensions, and the crowd stands in it anyway.
stops.quote: La proscripción perpetua es, en realidad, la pena principal. La privación de la libertad por seis años es sólo la accesoria.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Carta abierta: El costo democrático de la politización de la justicia', cfkargentina.com, 29 July 2026
suggested_refs: The apartment commonly reported as San José 1111, Constitución, Buenos Aires

stops.name: San José 1111, Buenos Aires: the Day of Peronist Loyalty
stops.date_confidence: attested; the text is published on cfkargentina.com under this date and was fetched directly
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of October, eighty years after the descamisados filled the Plaza de Mayo to get Perón out of Martín García, she publishes a message to her compañeros from house arrest. She sets the American ambassador of 1945 against the American treasury secretary of 2025 and puts the country in the same sentence it was put in then. Nine days later the election is held. She cannot be a candidate in it, having been disqualified for life, and the message is the whole of her campaign.
stops.quote: Exactamente 80 años después, otra vez nos ponen en la misma disyuntiva. En aquel entonces: era Braden o Perón. Hoy pareciera ser Bessent o Perón.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Mensaje a mis compañeros y compañeras en el Día de la Lealtad Peronista', cfkargentina.com, 17 October 2025
suggested_refs: The Day of Peronist Loyalty message of 17 October 2025, published from house arrest
sources: juan_peron.journey.json (Plaza de Mayo, the balcony and the descamisados, 1945-10-17)

stops.name: San José 1111, Buenos Aires: the letter to the United Nations
stops.date_confidence: attested; the open letter carries this date on cfkargentina.com and was fetched directly, and the Buenos Aires Times reports the accompanying petition to the UN Human Rights Committee
stops.campa: She publishes an open letter and takes the conviction to the Human Rights Committee of the United Nations, arguing that the lifetime ban is the sentence and the six years are the accessory to it. She is seventy-three and has been a provincial deputy, an interim governor, a national deputy, a senator three times over, a president twice, and a vice president, and is now none of these and cannot become any of them again. She is alive, with no tomb yet, only an address in Constitución and a website she keeps herself.
stops.quote: Hoy me dirijo a cada argentina y a cada argentino con la serenidad de quien sabe que la verdad tiene una fuerza que ninguna operación política, ninguna campaña de difamación y ninguna sentencia injusta podrán derrotar para siempre.
stops.quote_source: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, 'Carta abierta: El costo democrático de la politización de la justicia', cfkargentina.com, 29 July 2026
suggested_refs: The petition to the UN Human Rights Committee, 2026; cfkargentina.com as a self-curated archive
